verdict.rationale: Viam documents headless, scriptable operation. Its official CLI can call any machine API method with JSON in and JSON out, and the docs present it as a complete way to operate a machine from a shell. Agents with a shell or SDK can operate machines, the fleet API mirrors the web UI in code, and viam-server can run from a fake config without hardware. missing for 10: explicit CI-pipeline documentation or examples, documented non-interactive auth (e.g. API keys) for CI runners, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The CLI can call any API method a machine serves, with JSON in and JSON out. That makes it a complete way to operate a machine from a shell
An AI agent with a shell or an SDK can operate a Viam machine the same way a person or a program can.
The fleet management API allows you to manage your machine fleet with code the same way you can do in the web UI.
Example with a dummy configuration: `go run ./web/cmd/server -config etc/configs/fake.json`.
